summary:
SOLARIS is an interactive, browser-based space exploration platform designed to make planetary science engaging through 3D environments and educational mission-style activities.

It features three explorable worlds: Earth, the Moon, and Mars. The Mars environment includes activities involving spectrometry concepts, drilling, MOXIE-based oxygen production concepts, and solar energy. The Moon environment features a simulated lunar base with activities involving pressure balancing, dust management, communications, and drilling. Earth offers an interactive futuristic exploration environment with movement, boosts, and jumps. A built-in science assistant provides educational information using a locally stored knowledge base.

SOLARIS aims to make space science accessible, encourage curiosity, and introduce users to the challenges of future lunar and Martian exploration. It also introduces the concept of Earth analogues.

The project was developed using React, TypeScript, Three.js, React Three Fiber, Zustand, Framer Motion, and Vite, with AI-assisted coding tools.

Currently, SOLARIS is an educational platform, not a validated scientific Earth-analogue identification system or live NASA data-analysis tool. Future improvements could include NASA datasets, environmental comparisons, similarity scoring, and interactive mapping.

Live Website: https://solaris-eight-nu.vercel.app
details:
SOLARIS is an interactive, browser-based space exploration and educational platform designed to make planetary science more engaging through immersive digital environments and mission-style activities.

The platform features three explorable environments: Earth, the Moon, and Mars. Users can explore these environments and interact with educational activities inspired by the challenges of future space exploration.

The Mars environment includes activities involving spectrometry concepts, drilling, MOXIE-based oxygen production concepts, and solar energy. The Moon environment features a simulated lunar base with activities involving pressure balancing, dust management, communications, and drilling. The Earth environment provides an interactive futuristic exploration setting with movement, jumping, boosts, and environmental elements. SOLARIS also includes a built-in science assistant that retrieves educational information from a locally stored knowledge base.

The project aims to make space science more accessible, encourage scientific curiosity, and introduce users to the environmental and operational challenges of lunar and Martian exploration. It connects with the concept of Earth analogues by helping users understand the environments that future explorers may need to study and prepare for.

SOLARIS was developed using React, TypeScript, Three.js, React Three Fiber, Zustand, Framer Motion, and Vite. AI-assisted coding tools were also used during development.

The project is currently an educational exploration platform. It does not yet perform validated scientific identification or ranking of Earth-analogue locations, nor does it currently implement a live NASA data-analysis pipeline. Future development could integrate NASA datasets, environmental comparisons, transparent similarity scoring, and interactive geographical mapping.

The project is publicly deployed and accessible through its website:
https://solaris-eight-nu.vercel.app
